newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends mostly down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended mostly down on Wednesday on stop-loss orders and trading was sluggish on weak market sentiment after heavy losses on Tuesday, traders said.
The most active July 1997 contract ended at 22,760 yuan ($2,743) per tonne, losing 70 yuan. It opened at 22,950 yuan, hitting an intraday high of 23,000 and a low of 22,750 yuan.
April rose 110 yuan to 23,070, May 10 to 22,920, June fell 130 to 22,800, August 100 to 22,750, September 40 to 22,760.
Combined volume fell sharply to 46,230 tonnes from 113,660 tonnes.
Copper opened higher but stop-loss selling pushed prices down for most of the session.
Traders said the trend was not optimistic with few investors willing to buy at current levels.
"Copper met strong selling pressure at high levels on weak sentiment," one trader said. "Few investors want to build positions as most of them are pessimistic about which way the market will go."
Traders said copper was likely to fall further in the short term.
"There is no hope for copper to recover its losses in the short term -- that's what today's performance indicates," a second trader said. "Technical charts also indicate falls in the next few days."
Aluminium ended mixed in slow trading. April did not trade, May rose 50 yuan to 15,450 per tonne and June fell 40 to 15,600 yuan per tonne. Combined volume fell to 580 tonnes from 3,840.
